body.statement:
Under the formal specialization of the displayed constructions to \(m=1\), one has \(B=A\) and \(Q=D\). Consequently, \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) is empty when \((B,Q)\) violates any fine-grid compatibility constraint and otherwise equals the singleton \(\{(B,Q)\}\). Accordingly, on an admissible exact input the certificate returns incompatibility in the first case, while in the second case it returns the unique transfer
\[
h_{uv}(z)=\frac{B_{vu}z}{1-B_{vv}z},
\]
which is the standard unaliased direct process transfer.
body.justification: This verifies that the new machinery collapses to the familiar fine-grid formula when aliasing is removed.
body.gap: The reduction is not a novelty claim; it is the required fidelity check against standard process-graph transfer analysis.
body.consumer: Implementers can test the certificate against an unaliased benchmark before using it on subsampled data.
body.proof_tex:
Formally specialize Definitions~\(\texttt{def:compatible-fiber}\) and \(\texttt{def:certificate}\) to \(m=1\). Let \((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\). The first compatibility equation in Definition~\(\texttt{def:compatible-fiber}\) gives
\[
B=A^1=A.
\]
The second compatibility equation in that definition, together with \(A^0=I_d\), gives
\[
Q=\sum_{r=0}^{1-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top
  =A^0D(A^0)^\top
  =D.
\]
Thus every member of \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) equals \((B,Q)\), and the fiber has at most one member.

Conversely, substitute \((A,D)=(B,Q)\) into Definition~\(\texttt{def:compatible-fiber}\). The two coarse equations hold identically because \(B^1=B\) and
\[
\sum_{r=0}^{0}B^rQ(B^r)^\top=B^0Q(B^0)^\top=Q.
\]
The remaining conditions in that definition hold if and only if
\[
B_{ij}=0\quad(i<j),
\qquad
B_{ij}=0\quad(i>j\ \text{and}\ j\to i\notin G),
\]
\[
\max_i|B_{ii}|<1,
\qquad
Q_{ij}=0\quad(i\ne j),
\qquad
Q\succ0.
\]
These are exactly the fine-grid compatibility constraints obtained by the stated formal specialization. Therefore
\[
\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=
\begin{cases}
\{(B,Q)\},&\text{if all of the displayed compatibility constraints hold},\\
\varnothing,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

It remains to verify the asserted algorithmic output. Under \(m=1\), each enumerated diagonal-root equation is
\[
a_{ii}^{1}=B_{ii},
\]
and hence has the unique real solution \(a_{ii}=B_{ii}\). The declared divided-difference polynomial satisfies
\[
C_1(x,y)=\sum_{r=0}^{0}x^r y^{0-r}=1.
\]
Moreover, a nondecreasing walk of length one has at most one strict increase, whereas the declared remainder contains only monomials indexed by walks with at least two strict increases. Hence every such remainder at this specialization is zero. The lower-triangular root identity processed by the graph recursion consequently reduces, at each allowed off-diagonal coordinate, to
\[
B_{ij}=A_{ij}C_1(A_{ii},A_{jj})+0=A_{ij}.
\]
Thus no divided-difference coefficient is singular, and the recursive enumeration has the unique transition candidate \(A=B\). The coarse covariance equation then has the unique innovation candidate \(D=Q\). By Definition~\(\texttt{def:certificate}\), its exact compatibility test rejects this candidate exactly when it fails one of the defining constraints of \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\). The fiber characterization above therefore implies that the certificate returns incompatibility precisely when \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=\varnothing\), and otherwise accepts the unique compatible pair \((B,Q)\).

In the latter case, two compatible copies in the certificate's transfer-inequality test must both equal \((B,Q)\), so no two transfer-distinct witnesses exist. The certificate therefore returns the common transfer, which by the declared definition of \(h_{uv}\) is
\[
h_{uv}(z)=\frac{A_{vu}z}{1-A_{vv}z}
          =\frac{B_{vu}z}{1-B_{vv}z}.
\]
Compatibility gives \(|B_{vv}|<1\). Since \(z\in\mathbb T\) entails \(|z|=1\),
\[
|B_{vv}z|=|B_{vv}|<1,
\]
and therefore \(1-B_{vv}z\ne0\). The returned rational function is consequently well defined on \(\mathbb T\); because \(A=B\), it is exactly the unaliased direct fine-grid process transfer. This proves the proposition.
